meta.probingQuestion: Can you stay when leaving would be easier?

games.title: Chest to Chest Under Elbows Maintenance

meta.connection: Staying with a hard partner on the mat instead of switching is commitment made physical. Staying in a hard relationship when leaving is easier is the same choice. Both build the muscle of not bailing on people.
meta.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, open guard, and a chest-to-chest pin. Staying with a hard partner is commitment made physical, building the muscle of not bailing on people. That works off the mat too. You get to choose to stay on purpose, or leave if it's harmful.

slides.title: Can you stay when leaving would be easier?

body.text: This is using an underhook for a leg.

items: The attacker wins only by picking up the defender's leg, from any connection.
The defender wins by stopping the attacker for 30 seconds.

body.text: This is keeping your feet on him, close.

items: The bottom player holds as long as he keeps the connection.
The top player wins by getting outside the bottom player's legs and touching his body with a shin.

body.text: This is staying on top, under his elbows.

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps both of the bottom player's elbows covered.
The bottom player wins by getting both elbows to touch his body, or by making the top player fall.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: Your partner is standing to pass, and your feet are still hooked on him. What's the smart move?

options.text: Keep both feet hooked on him no matter what.
options.feedback: Staying connected under pressure is commitment made physical, the same choice as staying when leaving is easier.

options.text: Let your feet go and scramble up to stand.
options.feedback: Letting go here gives up your only connection.

options.text: Hold still and hope he stops moving.
options.feedback: Keep your feet hooked instead of hoping.
